title: Solbeck House, 3037 Dabbert Drive, Porter, Porter County, IN
notes: Significance: Built ca. 1930, the Solbeck site, including the house and landscape, is significant for its association with patterns of historical development and distinctive design characteristics indicative of the region. It was built as a vacation cottage along the lake shore in the area known as Porter Beach, a resort development that flourished during the 1920s and 1930s. The house is an excellent example of the Craftsman-influenced, vernacular beach property that was common in the Indiana Dunes during that period, but that has rarely survived in an unaltered state. The modest, vernacular cottages built at Porter Beach are similar to many of the pre-World War II cottages built in and around the cities of Gary and Michigan City, Indiana. By contrast, most of the houses built in the nearby communities of Dune Acres and Beverly Shores are more substantial and stylish. There are few if any of this type of property extant in the Indiana Dunes that compare to the Solbeck site for integrity of both structure and landscape setting. It was used as a beach cottage until 1952.
